chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Los Angeles Local 47 backs him; a paid vacation and the Ali-Liston fight
summary: The union tells him to keep showing up so he gets his pay and plane fare, and he spends three weeks with Kenny, Nancy Wilson's husband.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So I went to the Musicians Union, and I have to say that's one of the few times that the union has really proved to be on my side of the fence. I went to the Musicians Union, and I can't say enough for the local in Los Angeles -- I think it's Local 47. I went and expressed my case to them, and they told me, "Don't worry about a thing. You go back to your hotel, and go to work tonight, just like you were going, and if she doesn't want you to play, you stay there for an hour, and then go back to your hotel or wherever you want to go." So I did this for a couple of nights, and each day I would approach her. What happened, after about three days, he said, "You don't even need to go over there any more. Just stay around until the end of the engagement, and you will get your money and your plane fare back home."

So this I did, and while I was there, I have to say it proved out to be a very nice three-week vacation in California at Gloria Lynne's expense, and I had my plane fare back. I had a good time, because there were a lot of musicians that I knew out there that I hung out with. One of the guys that I

did a lot of hanging out with was a fellow named Kenny, who at that particular time was Nancy Wilson's husband. We went and saw the Muhammad Ali fight -- I think it was one of the major fights of his career -- with Sonny Liston. There were just so many things that happened...
